sections.html:
Herriman sits in the southwest corner of Salt Lake County, next to Riverton, South Jordan and Bluffdale. The city counted 1,523 residents in 2000, 21,785 in 2010 and 55,144 in 2020, and the latest estimate is 63,282 for July 1, 2025. Because most homes here were built in that boom, buyers often compare a listing against houses only a few years old.

sections.h2: Newer homes and what they mean for your sale
sections.html: Newer construction usually brings fewer old-house surprises. A house with a tenant, a title tangle or unfinished work stands out in that setting, and financed buyers tend to skip it. The city kept annexing land as it grew, most recently the 933-acre Olympia development in 2022, so more new houses keep arriving to compete with yours.

The city has no post office of its own. Mail runs through the Riverton Post Office at 12760 S 2080 W, so double-check the address on closing papers. City Hall is at 5355 West Herriman Main Street and keeps weekday hours from 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

Herriman City runs the water department. Other services come from separate providers, and you will move these accounts at closing.

  • Water: billed around the 10th of each month and due at month end, with a 1.5% late charge starting the second day after the due date.
  • Garbage: Wasatch Front Waste and Recycling.
  • Sewer: Jordan Basin Improvement District.
  • Fire: Unified Fire.
  • Schools: Jordan School District.

A new water account carries a $200 deposit, refunded after 24 months when there are no more than two late payments. A buyer new to town may ask whether your account is current.

Secondary water is a separate pressurized irrigation line for lawns and gardens, supplied by the Herriman City Water Department. It usually runs from early May to mid-October and then shuts down in stages.

To hook up, the owner has the sprinkler connection inspected, hands in a backflow test report if the yard also uses culinary water, and asks the city to set a secondary meter. The city installs the meter. A filter is smart because the water is filtered only to 200 microns.

If your yard still runs on culinary water, or the connection never passed inspection, expect questions from a buyer or inspector. The fix is simple, and a clean record spares you a delay.

Herriman is described as highly exposed to fire, with mountains, dry brush and open fields at its edges. A 2010 blaze that began during a National Guard exercise at nearby Camp Williams burned about 3,500 acres.

Utah's House Bill 48 of 2025 produced a statewide map rating buildings from 1 (lowest) to 8 (highest) for wildfire exposure. About 60,000 buildings statewide landed in the high-risk group, and those owners may face an annual state fee once the program starts. Type your address into wildfirerisk.utah.gov to see your score before a buyer does.

Herriman permits an internal accessory dwelling unit, called an I-ADU, only inside a single-family home, and only one per lot. The owner has to live on the property, either in the main house or in the unit.

  • The unit needs its own exterior entrance with a hard-surface walkway.
  • The application review fee is $559, plus a building permit fee that varies with the remodeled area.
  • Plan review takes about 7 to 14 business days.
  • The owner signs a notarized affidavit, which is recorded with the County Recorder.
  • After a passed inspection and an approval letter, the owner needs a business license before renting.

Work done without a permit may need drywall and insulation pulled out for inspection. If your basement apartment was finished on the quiet, weigh that cost before you list.

Salt Lake County sets the calendar. Valuation notices are mailed July 22, and the Board of Equalization hears appeals from August 1 to September 15. Tax notices go out November 1, payment is due November 30, and unpaid current-year taxes turn delinquent on December 1.

A primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value under the 45% state exemption. Appeals cover market value only, so gather comparable sales or an appraisal before the window closes.

The Salt Lake County Recorder files your deed for a flat $40, with up to ten legal descriptions included before extra charges apply. The document needs a notary acknowledgment and the tax serial number for each parcel. Your title company normally handles the filing right after closing.

sections.h2: Preparing a Herriman house for sale
sections.html:
Start with the paper trail. Find the permit and approval letter for any basement unit, the recorded affidavit if you have one, and the business license if you rented the space. Pull up your secondary water records so you can show the yard connection passed inspection.

Next, check your wildfire score and the age of the roof, then settle any water account balance so the buyer inherits a clean file. Walk the exterior and the yard the way an inspector would, noting anything a buyer might raise. Fixing a small thing now is cheaper than negotiating over it later. If a repair feels too big or too costly, that is the moment to consider a sale as-is, where the buyer takes the house in its present condition and you skip the project entirely.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Herriman?
sections.html:
With no lender involved, the schedule depends on title work and not on someone else's loan approval.

  1. Give us the address and a few details.
  2. We look over the house and recent sales close by.
  3. You say yes or no to the offer.
  4. A title company clears the record and fixes the closing date.
  5. The deed is recorded and the proceeds reach you at closing.

A half-finished I-ADU, a secondary water problem or a late tax bill can scare off a buyer who needs a loan. We buy the house as it stands, so those items get settled at closing and not before you list.

You will not wait on a lender's appraisal, and you will not pay for repairs that a bank would demand. Showings, staging and open-house weekends are optional too. The title company still orders a search, collects any payoff for taxes or a mortgage and prepares the papers. If the house sits in a family trust or an estate, mention that when you first call.

faqs.a: Salt Lake County. Herriman sits in the southwest part of the county, so the county assessor, treasurer and recorder handle your parcel.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Herriman?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay without penalty. Unpaid taxes are delinquent from December 1.

faqs.q: Can I rent out a basement apartment in Herriman?
faqs.a: Yes, if the home is a single-family house and the owner lives on the property. Herriman requires an I-ADU permit, a notarized affidavit recorded with the county, a passed final inspection and a business license before renting.
Jordan School District. Herriman has two high schools, Herriman High and Mountain Ridge High.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: The flat recording fee is $40, plus $2 for each legal description beyond ten. The document needs a notary acknowledgment and the tax serial number of each parcel.
